$comment: Being free to do something, because no duty forbids it. A liberty is the absence of a duty, and that is its whole content — which is why it is named against duty and why it carries no prefix: nothing else in the enterprise is called a liberty. A liberty is not a right. Your liberty to do a thing does not oblige anyone to let you: it means only that you do no wrong by doing it. The property owner has a claim that strangers not trespass AND a liberty to use the land; a stranger has the liberty to look at it but not to enter. Hohfeld called this 'privilege' and it was his worst word — in ordinary English a privilege is an unearned advantage, which is nearly the opposite. His successors say liberty. So do we.

name.$comment: What the liberty is called, as it is said.

under.$comment: The authority under which no duty forbids it. Being free of a duty under one authority is not being free of it under another.

free-to.$comment: The work you do no wrong by doing. Names a work and must resolve to one.

against.$comment: Who cannot complain of it. They hold the matching no-claim: if you are free to do it, they have no claim on you that you not. A liberty against nobody is not a liberty — there is no one it is held against.

$comment-absences: No discharged-when: a liberty is not owed and is not discharged. Nothing settles it, because there is nothing to do — a liberty carrying discharge conditions has been mis-written as a duty. No holder or bearer: the office's deontic profile is where the holder enters.
